title: The Sages of the South
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman cites [Bava Batra 96a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.96a.6), where the southern sages teach in Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi’s name; [Jerusalem Talmud] [Pesachim 7:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Pesachim.7.7.8) has Resh Lakish objecting to the southern sages. [Zevachim 22b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.22b.9-12) cites “the elders of the south”; Ulla reports that Resh Lakish challenged them. Hyman cites Terumot 2:4. The corresponding [Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 2:2:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Terumot.2.2.5) and [Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 5:3:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Pesachim.5.3.3) introduce teachings from the southerners. In [Bereshit Rabbah 63:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.63.8) the southern sages cite Rabbi Alexandri. In [71:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.71.7) they cite Rabbi Alexandri, who cites Rabbi Yochanan. Hyman describes them as a group of sages living in Lod in the south, where R’ Yehoshua ben Levi and B-Q [the supplied abbreviation ב״ק] lived.[^4]

notes.text: The checked Bava Batra spells Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, not Yehudah ben Lakish. The final ב״ק may denote Bar Kappara, but that expansion is not established in this bounded reading and remains abbreviated.

The whole saved TE Bereshit Rabbah71:7 has southern rabbis in Rabbi Alexandri’s name in Rabbi Yochanan’s name, one connected chain. Hyman’s repeated71:7 references are retained as his citation list, not independent attestations. The63:8 passage and earlier Bava Batra/Yerushalmi comparisons are not newly inspected. Contextual Yehoshua ben Levi is not Yehudah ben Lakish; its abbreviated title stays R-prime without newly supplied full-title evidence. Final ב״ק remains unresolved, with Bar Kappara only a candidate. Lod residence and the group characterization remain Hyman’s claims, not a new roster.

Bava Batra 96a names Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, and both the Jerusalem Talmud (Pesachim 7:7) and Bavli (Zevachim 22b) describe Resh Lakish’s objection to the southerners. Bereshit Rabbah 63:8 gives the southern rabbis in Rabbi Alexandri’s name alongside a separate transmission through Rachava. The consulted 71:7 gives one chain through Rabbi Alexandri to Rabbi Yochanan. Hyman’s print (vol. I, p. 335) leaves ב״ק abbreviated. These passages attest the group’s teachings but do not fix the expansion or establish Hyman’s proposed Lod identification.

The two citations of [Bereshit Rabbah 71:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.71.7) point to a single chain. [63:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.63.8) separately includes a parallel transmission through Rachava.
